reason: The cited evidence (E1, E3, E4) discusses oxidation kinetics, oxide phases, and solid-solution strengthening in HEAs, but none addresses lamellar interface morphology, microcrack initiation, or serration-induced mechanical property improvements. The key premises about interface serration and its effects on strength and ductility are entirely unsupported by the provided passages.
premises: Smooth, straight lamellar interfaces in eutectic HEAs are prone to microcrack initiation under tensile loading
Serrated (tortuous) interfaces can blunt and deflect stress concentrations, delaying microcrack initiation and propagation
Irregular boundary topography promotes strain delocalization and additional strain hardening
A post-processing treatment (annealing/deformation) can transform smooth lamellar interfaces into a serrated morphology in eutectic HEAs
The combined effect of delayed cracking and enhanced strain hardening simultaneously improves strength and room-temperature tensile ductility
